subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should OpenClaw solve this as narrow per-job/heartbeat elevated approval state, or fold it into the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design?
rationale: The source gap is real, but choosing where trusted authority is created, stored, audited, migrated, and enforced changes the elevated host-exec trust boundary and compatibility behavior for existing cron/heartbeat users.

options.title: Fold into scheduling provenance
options.body: Treat elevated execution as part of the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design so cron APIs, heartbeat state, audit, and upgrade handling share one authority model.

options.title: Implement narrow elevated markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat-specific elevated approval metadata now, with execution-time checks and docs, while leaving broader scheduling provenance to a later RFC.

options.title: Fail closed for internal sources
options.body: Remove wildcard internal-source elevation by default and require explicit operator opt-in, accepting upgrade friction for existing cron/heartbeat setups.

recommendation.title: Fold into scheduling provenance
recommendation.body: Treat elevated execution as part of the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design so cron APIs, heartbeat state, audit, and upgrade handling share one authority model.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently owned the adjacent agent cron caller-scope implementation that already touched the Gateway, agent tool, protocol, and upgrade-proof surfaces this decision would extend.
